topline.theme: S184 closed the 'built-but-unproven' gap; S185 asked 'what converts?'. S186's thesis: the site now runs two rich loops that don't talk to each other. Loop A proves trust — status-proof.json carries a live trustScore, 99.x% uptime, a confirmed -46% LCP field-win. Loop B converts — adaptive-cta pathway notes, the Oracle/IGNIS answer engine, membership register. But the proof never reaches the CTA, the Oracle launches cold (0 organic queries), proactive hints fire unmeasured, and half-shipped instrumentation (geo-vitals colo workflow) leaves the global win unconfirmed. The genius move is to weld the two loops: pipe earned operational proof into the conversion surface, kill Oracle cold-start with real query clusters, and make every visitor interaction both measured and consequential. Plus finish the agent-executable security carry (TT named-policy on the last 2 first-party sinks) so the enforce-flip is a one-line founder yes.

founderEvidence: Goal-chain /start -> /audit -> /implement -> /closeout with explicit ask: genius-level creative thinking, personalized to THIS project's real lists/flags/blockers, with a post-closeout impact score. Personalization anchors: TASK_BOARD open carries (TT-ENFORCE 2 remaining first-party sinks, GEO-VITALS-COLO-PROBE-WORKFLOW, IGNIS-HINT-CONVERSION-TRACKING, CLOSEOUT-BUILD-ORDER-MODULE, PROGRESSIVE-MEMBERSHIP-UNLOCK, vaultsparked-proof.js delete); live evidence that adaptive-cta.js emits pathway 'note' lines (proof insertion point), ignis-answer-engine.js owns showHint() + the cold Oracle input, build-oracle-query-clusters.mjs already emits api/oracle-insights.json (11 clusters) + api/oracle-queries.json, and api/status-proof.json is deployed with a trustScore. Founder-gated items (RICHER-IGNIS-LAYER public-safe decision, TT enforce-FLIP per SOUL #3, nav-sheet device verify) are explicitly OUT of agent scope and listed as blocked.

items.summary: The site spent five sessions building proof feeds (status-proof.json: trustScore, uptime %, a confirmed -46% LCP field-win) but that earned proof lives only on /status/. Surface ONE live trust microline on the conversion surface, sourced from the deployed proof feed, so operational reliability becomes a conversion lever.
items.why: A studio that publishes its own SRE proof and then never shows it to the person deciding to sign up is leaving its strongest, most honest argument on the floor. Reading the single deployed status-proof.json and rendering a tiny verified line ('Backed by a studio measured at NN% uptime, -46% faster than last quarter') next to the register CTA turns a trust artifact into a conversion argument no other studio site makes. Conversion outcome: the membership/register CTA carries live, earned, falsifiable proof at the exact moment of decision.
items.recipe: Add assets/proof-conversion-line.js (ambient-loader predicate: pages with a [data-vs-cta] or the /vault-member register surface, NOT '/' which is prove-first per S123). Fetch the deployed /api/status-proof.json (graceful no-op on miss), pull worstStale<threshold + uptime % + the confirmed field-win delta, and inject a single muted microline into the adaptive-cta 'note' slot (extend applyPathwayConfig output with an optional proofLine, rendered only when fresh). Honest-dark: render nothing if the proof is stale or trustScore is low (never fabricate confidence). Cost-neutral (static CDN fetch). Add a vs:ux 'proof-line-shown' event so lift is measurable.

items.summary: The Oracle / IGNIS answer engine launches cold with an empty input and gets 0 queries from organic visits. build-oracle-query-clusters.mjs already emits api/oracle-insights.json (11 real clusters). Seed the empty state with 3 dynamically-chosen one-tap question chips so a visitor's first interaction is a click, not a typed query.
items.why: Cold text inputs are the highest-friction first interaction on the web, and a brand-anchor site whose intelligence layer gets zero organic use is a feature paying rent in bytes and earning nothing. Seeding the empty state from the real query clusters means the chips are honest (they reflect what the corpus can actually answer) and self-maintaining (regenerated by the existing build). Info-finding outcome: first-query rate moves off zero because the cheapest path to an answer is one tap.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js, on mount when the input is empty, fetch /api/oracle-insights.json (or oracle-queries.json) and render the top 3 clusters by weight as <button> chips beneath the input; clicking a chip fills + submits the query. Reuse the existing answer pipeline (no new backend). TT-safe (named policy, no innerHTML on untrusted strings — chip text is from our own build). Emit vs:ux 'oracle-chip-shown' / 'oracle-chip-click' so chip-driven query rate is measurable. Empty/failed fetch => no chips (graceful).

items.summary: Oracle proactive hints fire (showHint() in ignis-answer-engine.js) but shown/dismissed/clicked are all unmeasured, so we cannot tell whether the hint feature drives Oracle usage. Instrument it with vs:ux events mirroring the nav-sheet telemetry pattern.
items.why: You cannot improve a funnel you cannot see, and right now the proactive-hint -> Oracle-query path is completely dark. Adding three lightweight events closes the loop that ignis-answer-seeded-empty-state opens, so next session can compare chip-driven vs hint-driven first queries with real numbers. Info-finding outcome: the hint feature becomes a measured funnel instead of a guess.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js showHint(): dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('vs:ux',{detail:{type:'ignis-hint',action:'shown'},bubbles:true})); add matching action:'dismissed' on the dismiss handler and action:'click' on the hint click-through. Confirm the existing RUM beacon (/v/rum) already forwards vs:ux events (nav-sheet pattern) so no new transport is needed. Cost-neutral.

items.summary: The feedback-decision-board exists, but a visitor who submits feedback never sees it ship. Build a public 'shipped from feedback' receipt that maps feedback themes to shipped commits using the existing Forge Ledger / commit-map infra, closing the loop visibly.
items.why: Feedback that vanishes trains visitors to stop giving it; feedback that visibly ships trains them to return and trust. The studio already computes a commit map and a Forge Ledger, so the data to draw 'you asked, we shipped' lines already exists and just needs a public-safe rendering. Conversion outcome: submitting feedback becomes a reason to come back, turning a one-way form into a retention loop.
items.recipe: Add scripts/build-feedback-receipts.mjs that joins public feedback themes (existing feedback-decision-board source) to shipped commits via the commit-map, writes api/feedback-receipts.json (public-safe, no internal text), and surface a compact 'Shipped from feedback' strip on the feedback page reading that feed. Wire into build + build:check drift gate. Honest-dark when no confirmed mappings exist.

items.summary: TT-ENFORCE-REPROBE is blocked on the last first-party default-policy sinks: home-idle-loader.js:16, schema-injector.js:23, and ambient.shell. Migrate them to named Trusted-Types policies (the S185 named-policy wave pattern), then reprobe and write a dated readiness verdict.
items.why: Trusted-Types enforcement is the single biggest hardening available to a static site's DOM-injection surface, and it is gated only by a handful of first-party sinks the agent can migrate. Doing the migration + reprobe leaves only the SOUL #3 device-verified flip for the founder, shrinking a multi-session security carry to a one-line yes. Security outcome: the auth/signup DOM surface moves from 'default policy, unenforceable' to 'named-policy, enforce-ready'.
items.recipe: Apply the S185 named-policy pattern (lint-tt-policies.mjs is the gate) to home-idle-loader.js:16 and schema-injector.js:23 — give each a file-specific named policy (vs-home-idle, vs-schema-inject) instead of the shared default. Audit ambient.shell's remaining default-policy use and name it. Run node scripts/probe-tt-soak.mjs && node scripts/analyze-tt-violations.mjs, capture the new cluster count into docs/TT_ENFORCE_READINESS_2026-06-11.md with a GREEN/AMBER verdict + the exact flip command. Do NOT flip (founder-device gated per SOUL #3). Update the TASK_BOARD carry with the dated result + the football-gm Ark cargo status.

items.summary: S185 wave4c shipped the colo-probe code (probe-uptime.mjs --colo-probe) but never wired the GH Actions trigger, so the global confirmation of the -46% LCP origin-migration win (US:107 vs GB:3 samples) cannot accrue. Wire the workflow trigger.
items.why: A field win confirmed only in one region is a hypothesis everywhere else, and the probe that would settle it is already written and just not scheduled. Adding the workflow step costs an hour and converts a P3 watch into accruing global evidence. Info-finding outcome: api/geo-vitals.json starts gathering non-US samples so the next session can confirm or regress-hunt the global win.
items.recipe: Add a step (or scheduled matrix entry) to .github/workflows/uptime-probe.yml invoking node scripts/probe-uptime.mjs --colo-probe, committing api/geo-vitals.json low-churn ([skip ci] only on no-state-change, matching the S178 uptime pattern). Validate the YAML with npx --yes js-yaml on the file before push (per the workflow-YAML-validation memory). Confirm the rebase-before-push guard is already present (S184 added it to the 7 self-committing workflows).

items.summary: The deferred Wave-5 UX item: reveal membership value progressively as a visitor demonstrates engagement (visit depth, returning), instead of a flat all-at-once pitch. Ship a scoped Wave-1 slice this session if budget allows; otherwise keep as the named next-session anchor.
items.why: A flat membership pitch treats a first-touch stranger and a fourth-visit regular identically, wasting the engagement signal the site already tracks (returning-visitor digest, visit depth). Progressive disclosure tied to demonstrated interest is how the best product sites convert without nagging. Conversion outcome: the membership ask escalates with earned intent, so high-intent returners see the deeper pitch and cold arrivals are not over-asked.
items.recipe: Wave-1 slice: gate ONE incremental membership detail (e.g. the deeper tier note) behind the existing returning-visitor / visit-depth signal already in localStorage, reusing the adaptive-cta pathway state — no new tracking. Behind a ?param/localStorage flag (flag-gated UX swap on a mature surface per project convention) and graduate via founder real-device verification. Full 8h build stays the next-session anchor.

items.summary: The oracle -> shards -> ledger build ordering lives inline in closeout-autopilot step3d.7. Extract it into scripts/lib/build-order.mjs so it is canonical and importable, preventing ordering drift if step3d.7 is edited.
items.why: Build-ordering logic buried in a 3000-line autopilot step is one careless edit away from silently producing stale derived feeds. Pulling it into a named, self-testing module makes the ordering a contract instead of a convention. Maintainability outcome: any script that regenerates derived feeds imports one ordering source of truth.
items.recipe: Create scripts/lib/build-order.mjs exporting the ordered build sequence (oracle feed -> llms shards -> forge ledger -> dependent renders) with a small self-test; refactor closeout-autopilot step3d.7 to import + call it. No behavior change — pure extraction. Verify build:check stays green.

items.summary: node scripts/ops.mjs doctor reports 11/13 passing + 1 advisory drift + 1 warning, with 2 stale sibling session locks among 15. Triage: clear what is genuinely local (advisory drift) and confirm the sibling-lock warning is cross-repo noise, not a this-repo health gap.
items.why: A persistent doctor warning erodes the signal value of the whole probe — once one warning is 'normal', a real one hides in plain sight. An hour of triage either clears it or proves it is external, restoring the green baseline the startup brief depends on. Health outcome: the doctor probe returns to a trustworthy all-clear (or documents exactly why a warning is expected).
items.recipe: Run node scripts/ops.mjs doctor with full output, identify the advisory-drift probe + the warning source. If the warning is stale sibling session locks (cross-repo), confirm and document it as expected noise (not this repo's concern). Fix the local advisory drift if it is a real this-repo gap. Re-run to confirm 13/13 or a documented expected-warning state.

items.summary: assets/vaultsparked-proof.js is flagged evidence-complete for deletion (6-8d on the founder-unlocks list). Verify it is truly orphaned (no live references) and remove it, shedding a dead bundle.
items.why: Dead assets are small individually but compound into the 'redundant + slow' pain that subtractive audits exist to address, and this one is already marked evidence-complete. Removing it is the cheapest possible hygiene win once orphan-status is confirmed. Maintainability outcome: one fewer dead file in the asset corpus and the orphan checker stays honest.
items.recipe: Grep the full corpus (HTML, ambient shells, propagate-nav, service worker STATIC_ASSETS) for vaultsparked-proof.js references. If zero live references, git rm it and re-run the corpus-aware orphan checker + build:check. If ANY reference exists, leave it and report the contradiction (do not delete something still wired). The nav-sheet device-verify half of this carry stays founder-gated.
